governance.determination: REJECTED PROBE (mechanism confirmed, insufficient alone). Keeper stays nyiso-27 cc-offer (keepers.json[NYISO] unchanged).
governance.note: Re-solve of the nyiso-27 cc-offer keeper config (byte-identical keeper flags: --gas-monthly-actuals --gas-hub-basis-overlay --gas-hub-basis-daily --priced-interchange --energy-reserve-coopt --nyiso-local-selfsupply --nyiso-firm-imports --nyiso-import-reconciliation; P1, no commitment) plus ONE new NYISO-only, default-OFF source lever: --nyiso-synchronised-reserve. The lever adds a NYC 10-minute SYNCHRONISED (spinning) reserve sub-requirement = NYISO_SPIN_FRACTION x the NYC 10-min total = 0.5 x 500 = 250 MW (the published NYISO 1/2-largest-contingency rule, the SAME 1/2 rule that fixes nyca_10min_spin = 655 MW; a measured market-design constant, NOT fitted to any residual). It is supplied by a third reserve class -- the quick-start subset again, but ONLINE-bounded: dispatch._build_reserve_rows adds a per-zone row R[c,z] <= sum_g P[g] for the spinning class, so only ALREADY-GENERATING capacity counts, on top of the standard headroom row (R <= cap - P). The effective bound R <= min(P, cap - P) forces idle NYC peakers to COMMIT (generate >= the spin) to hold the requirement -- attacking PR #877's confirmed root cause (the pure-ED LP credits an idle peaker's full pmax as deliverable reserve, P=0 => R=cap, so the downstate families never bind). This is path A (the LP-linear online proxy, PR #877 recommendation #2), tested first to de-risk the heavier path B (zonal/family commitment, recommendation #1). PURPOSE: confirm whether forcing online-only spin moves CT_PEAKER / C3c / C3a in the right direction.
governance.validation_note: No scored OUTPUT is pinned and NO price adder is added -- the >$300 tail in this run is whatever the binding reserve family endogenously produces (here: it does NOT fire, see below). The single new quantity is a measured INPUT: the spinning fraction 0.5 (NYISO Ancillary Services / T&D Operations Manual: 10-min spinning = 1/2 largest contingency), applied to the already-grounded NYC 10-min total requirement -- forward-reproducible and not tuned to the NYISO price/volume residual. The fraction was set TO the published rule (0.5), NOT raised to whatever value would manufacture the missing tail hours (forbidden, rule #12). The gas total and LMP remain unpinned; no unit pinned to CEMS; no haircut/adder/sigmoid tuned to a residual; the td_loss / gas-basis floor is untouched.

_probe_outcome: REJECTED PROBE -- the synchronised-reserve mechanism is CONFIRMED but INSUFFICIENT ALONE, exactly as PR #877 (docs/handoffs/nyiso-downstate-reserve-incidence-2026-06.md) predicted for path A. EVIDENCE vs the nyiso-27 keeper: (a) MECHANISM CONFIRMED -- forcing the NYC quick-start fleet online to hold the 250 MW spin lifts CT_PEAKER toward 0 (C1 CT_PEAKER 2023 -1.30 -> -0.92 TWh, 2024 -1.51 -> -1.05 TWh) and relieves the complementary CC over-displacement (C1 CC_REGULAR 2023 +1.65 -> +1.36, 2024 +2.00 -> +1.43 TWh) -- the predicted CT_PEAKER up / CC over-run down signs. (b) INSUFFICIENT FOR THE TAIL -- C3c >$300 hours are UNCHANGED (2023 1, 2024 0, 2025 8; identical to the keeper) and C3a mean LMP slightly REGRESSES (2024 -9.7% -> -11.0%). ROOT CAUSE of the insufficiency (PR #877's explicit prediction): the grounded 250 MW NYC spin is small enough that the online quick-start fleet covers it CHEAPLY -- the spinning family clears at a low reserve price, never firing the >$300 RCPF step -- and the peakers that commit for spin add low-cost pmin energy in NON-scarce hours, which dilutes the mean (the small C3a dip). So online-only spin on the small grounded SUB-requirement moves the ENERGY frontier (CT_PEAKER/CC) but not the SCARCITY tail. This justifies and scopes path B: a commitment-aware ZONAL/FAMILY synchronised reserve where the FULL downstate 10-/30-min reserve stack (not just the 250 MW spin sub-slice) is satisfiable only by COMMITTED units, so the requirement actually BINDS against online headroom in tight hours and the RCPF dual stacks into the NYC LMP. The path-A lever (--nyiso-synchronised-reserve) is REVERTED on the branch (rejected probe; keeper stays nyiso-27); the full implementation is preserved in this bundle's model_changes.diff and the scope for B is docs/handoffs/nyiso-synchronised-reserve-probe-2026-06.md.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (NYC-peaker reserve/scarcity tail, incidence-gated; partially relieved by the synch-reserve probe)
exceptions.reason: CT_PEAKER under-runs because NYC peakers clear on reserve/scarcity, not energy. The synch-reserve probe forces ~0.4 TWh of the fleet online for the 250 MW NYC spin (the predicted relief, -1.30 -> -0.92), but the rest of the gap is the deeper scarcity-tail incidence that only the full path-B commitment-aware downstate reserve (where the whole 10-/30-min stack binds on committed-only headroom) can close. Lever reverted; keeper stays nyiso-27.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (NYC-peaker reserve/scarcity tail, incidence-gated; partially relieved by the synch-reserve probe)
exceptions.reason: Same NYC-peaker reserve/scarcity tail as 2023; the synch-reserve probe relieves it from -1.51 to -1.05 TWh by committing the NYC quick-start fleet for the 250 MW spin. The residual is the deeper scarcity-tail incidence (path B). Lever reverted; keeper stays nyiso-27.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (CC offer-level frontier at its grounded ceiling; complementary to CT_PEAKER)
exceptions.reason: CC over-runs because it sits at the CAMPD CC marginal-HR offer ceiling (nyiso-27 keeper attestation); the synch-reserve probe commits NYC peakers that displace a little marginal CC (+1.65 -> +1.36), the predicted CC-over-run-down sign. The residual is the converged CC offer level (out of scope here -- do not touch _NYISO_OFFER_CURVE; rule #12). Lever reverted; keeper stays nyiso-27.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (CC offer-level frontier at its grounded ceiling; complementary to CT_PEAKER)
exceptions.reason: Same CC offer-ceiling frontier as 2023; the synch-reserve probe's committed NYC peakers displace marginal CC (+2.00 -> +1.43). Converged CC offer level, out of scope (separate offer frontier). Lever reverted; keeper stays nyiso-27.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (within-gas merit residual at the grounded CC offer ceiling)
exceptions.reason: ST_GAS under-runs as the complement of the CC over-run at the grounded CC offer ceiling (nyiso-27 frontier). The synch-reserve probe shifts a little energy toward the committed peakers, leaving ST_GAS marginally lower (-1.27 -> -1.42). The within-gas merit ORDER stays physically correct (CC ahead of steam). Out of scope; not chased with an un-grounded knob. Lever reverted; keeper stays nyiso-27.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (within-gas merit residual + 2024 gas basis floor)
exceptions.reason: Same within-gas merit residual as 2023, amplified in 2024 by the EIA-930/EIA-923 gas-total basis floor (the gas family is total-constrained low, so the steam slice it leaves is correspondingly under; docs/nyiso-td-loss-resolution-2026-06.md). Essentially unchanged vs the keeper (-4.17 -> -4.30). Not closable without re-pinning the gas total (forbidden, rule #12). Lever reverted; keeper stays nyiso-27.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (downstream of the missing downstate scarcity tail)
exceptions.reason: The depressed mean is largely the missing >$300 downstate scarcity hours (C3c). The synch-reserve probe does NOT fire that tail (the 250 MW spin clears cheaply), and the committed peakers add low-cost pmin energy in non-scarce hours, so the mean does not recover (and dips slightly). The mean recovers only when the downstate reserve actually binds (path B). Not chased with a price adder (rule #12). Lever reverted; keeper stays nyiso-27.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (downstream of the missing downstate scarcity tail; mild probe regression)
exceptions.reason: Same mechanism as 2023: with the tail unfired, the committed-for-spin peakers add low-cost pmin energy in non-scarce hours and the mean dips from the keeper's -9.7% to -11.0%. This is a documented downside of path A WITHOUT the binding tail -- it is exactly why path A is a rejected probe and path B (binding the full downstate reserve) is required to lift the mean via real scarcity price formation, not added baseload. Not chased with an adder. Lever reverted; keeper stays nyiso-27.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (shape follows the missing scarcity tail)
exceptions.reason: The duration-curve shape misfit is dominated by the missing upper tail (the >$300 hours the model does not produce). The synch-reserve probe does not add those hours, so the shape is essentially unchanged (0.243 -> 0.250). Closes only when the tail fires endogenously (path B). Lever reverted; keeper stays nyiso-27.

exceptions.metric: C2 gas total vs EIA-923 grid-delivered
exceptions.reason: 2025 EIA-923 is the preliminary M-file (total under-reported); the gas gap is the EIA-930/EIA-923 basis reconciliation (docs/nyiso-td-loss-resolution-2026-06.md; td_loss_factor=0 settled) plus preliminary-data incompleteness, not a dispatch error. The synch-reserve probe is a within-fleet reshuffle (CC down, peaker up) and does not move the gas TOTAL, which sits at its basis floor. Not closable by an honest knob (rules #1/#11/#12).

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (downstream of the 2024 gas basis floor)
exceptions.reason: 2024 CO2 is downstream of the 2024 gas volume, which is at its EIA-923/EIA-930 basis floor. Unchanged in character vs the keeper; the synch-reserve probe shifts some energy from CC toward the dirtier-per-MWh peaker class (a small offsetting CO2 effect) but the level stays governed by the gas-total basis floor. Not a separate emission-rate error and not closable without re-pinning the gas total to actuals (forbidden, rule #12).
